statement: A frame has two names. Its head, the hash it is acked and chained by, is the digest of the dispute-proof message both sides sign: the Account's proof body after the frame, at the nonce the first signed frame's plus its height minus one, authored by the frame's proposer, so the bytes bind the author side, the state and the height. Its content name (author, parent, attempt, txs) needs no state, and a refusal, a repeat and the refusal memory use it, never the head; an ack names the head and one that names the content is ignored. A state that has no proof body is refused before anyone signs it (fault unsignable) and a frame whose digest cannot be made is refused with notice. Each replica builds both from its own state: nothing signed comes from the wire. Signing, and checking the signature before the memory is consulted, are the Runtime's (T0).
source: coordinator decision 10-01 on A3 (provisional frame hash)
